title: Make the ship phase observable before the next billed run

completion_criteria.text: The live GitHub lane executes for the first time and either passes, or its failure is traced to a named root cause at path and line rather than being retried.
A boundary gate that could not collect the sides it compares parks the unit with its own refusal text instead of dispatching a fix child into a directory that was never created.
The one real red on the trunk is cleared so a billed run starts from a green suite: the stale spawned-child assertion is corrected, without changing engine behaviour to make it pass.
The repeated live-run failure has a named root cause with evidence, and an approved non-ambiguous SPEC exists to extract mitosis into its own public repository as an installable plugin.
The four dispatch kinds that carry no unit become recordable, so ship and integrate can be replayed from real responses instead of hand-authored guesses.
The harness built-wait race is fixed and proven by a test red on the parent commit, so a billed run cannot be killed mid-flight and charged for nothing.
Teardown's unbounded directory removal is bounded across all three call sites, with a test proving a path outside the repository is refused.

spine.active_goal: Extract mitosis into its own public repository as an installable plugin, with a test architecture in which a green suite predicts live behaviour.
spine.next_step: START HERE. The extraction SPEC is approved. Plan the implementation of its sixteen units non-ambiguously: read the SPEC in full first, especially section 9 and U12's scope, then produce an execution plan with ordering, per-unit dispatch briefs, and the publication gate as a hard precondition. Open a child thread to carry the implementation; this thread does not. Do NOT execute units and do NOT run the engine - the migration is hand-executed by delegated agents per 0693.
spine.last_session: 2026-08-23: traced why a failed review parks, inverted the fanout premise, named the recurrence mechanism, audited the testing SPEC at 49 of 75 obligations met, and produced an approved 1,603-line extraction SPEC. No code changed and no billed run spent.

open_risks.text: Instrument the failing repository read before diagnosing another lane failure — an absent repository and one the token cannot see return the same empty result today
Preserve the untracked harness scripts holding the crash-point fix — no suite and no enforcer covers them, so the fix is invisible to CI and lost if that artifacts directory is cleared
Bound the two recursive removals still outside the bounded teardown — the same primitive is called directly elsewhere, so the containment already shipped does not reach them
Check whether remediation is merely unwired before calling the retry gap a defect — modules for planning and prompting a fix already exist in the tree
Do not treat the boundary reclaim fix as proven — the billed run never crashed, so the path it repairs was never entered
Prove crash recovery with a local zero-cost test rather than another billed run — a paid run only exercises the race when the timing happens to land
Read the run cost as a floor rather than a measurement — usage recorded one dispatch of four
Do not cite the declared-criteria comparison log for this run — it was never regenerated and still describes the previous one
Do not treat c2 as met at three of four kinds — decompose runs as its own process with no run store, so giving it one means fabricating a synthetic run and key
Treat recording as necessary but not sufficient for replay — the stub routes by live schema identity, so a cassette for an unrouted kind loads, is never consumed, and can still pass
Scope dispatch-kind work against twelve kinds — the code freezes twelve and refuses anything outside them, which closes the older eight-versus-twelve disagreement
Run the publication gate before the repository is ever public — a confidential codename appears 1,589 times in a gitignored template file, and a public push of it cannot be undone
Follow the SPEC's removal ordering exactly — a SessionStart hook hard-exits when the engine is absent, so a wrong order breaks every session on this machine
Treat the engine as untrusted for its own migration even after U12 lands — a fixed failed-review park is not a proven one, and the SPEC states this so it is not relitigated

Read this suite's verdict from CI rather than any local run — the primary checkout is the only honest local reader, a fresh clone adds fourteen false failures, and a linked worktree censuses an empty set
Treat a receipts check that clears in seconds as a downgrade or a skip — the word reverted matches a ladder tag and short-circuits all eight re-run gates, and a tests-only diff skips them by design
Expect a red pull request to merge on one click — this repository has no required status checks, which is how a stale assertion reached the trunk

Take a suite verdict from the fail count rather than the names in the failed log — todo-marked tests print there without counting, and reading them as failures produced a fix brief for a defect that did not exist

Check whether an existing test already asserts the defect before calling a fix complete — three tests across two sessions expected the broken behaviour outright, and a green suite over them hid every one

Declare work-type chore at creation on a config-only pull request — a toml file counts as source to the enforcer, and an inert work-type value is worse than none because it disables the config-only escape

key_decisions.title: Only work that moves the engine toward a completed live run gets done
Pre-create the harness repository instead of granting repository-creation rights
Decide the crash point from settled state instead of racing to win it
Park on a collection refusal rather than dispatching a child with nowhere to stand
The repeated creation error now means token visibility, not a missing repository
The live lane is blocked by fine-grained PAT visibility, not by a missing repository
Dispatch recording lands before the billed run; cassette harvest is deferred until after it
The two engine defects red on the trunk are fixed before the billed run, not filed
The six-versus-seven spawned-child count is a stale test expectation, not a regression
Honest inertness wording downgraded the receipts gate again; the downgrade is accepted, not re-litigated
The live GitHub lane passed for the first time, against a real repository, not a skip
Mitosis extracts to its own public repository as an installable plugin, migrated by hand
Adding fixture-backed tests is ruled out as the response to a mitosis defect

out_of_scope: Merging pull request 289, which is human-gated and never done from a session
Executing any of the sixteen extraction units; the successor session plans them and does not run them
